portada.subtitulo: Applied AI · Agents · MCP · Language models
portada.intro: For the past two years I've been building with AI: games that run language models locally, MCP servers that connect agents to real tools, agents that work every day, and voice, vision and 3D pipelines. I care about it working and costing what it should, so I measure every model before I commit to it.

bloques.texto: I edit video by talking to Claude Code. To avoid depending on a paid API, I wrote a local drop-in replacement for the transcription step with Whisper large-v3 on the GPU, returning exactly the format the editing tool expects.
Gesture control for smart lights: an ESP32 camera with infrared LEDs tracks the tip of a wand, and MediaPipe hand and pose detectors turn the movement into commands.
An agentic bot on a local language model that reads bug reports written in natural language, classifies them and files them by priority.

proyectos.tipo: Educational game with a local language model · Unity 6 · 2026
proyectos.rol: Developer: model integration and inference architecture
parrafos: A cyberpunk detective RPG for Spanish speakers learning English. Character interrogations, a translation minigame and the detective's narration are generated by a language model that returns typed JSON output.

I designed a common inference interface with swappable engines: Gemma running locally through Ollama in the editor, MediaPipe to run it on the Android phone itself, and a stub engine. When the model breaks the schema, a parser with three retries recovers the response. Prompts are templates the design team can edit, and text streams in.

proyectos.tipo: Talk at Interaction 2026 · Universidad Católica Luis Amigó · September 2026
parrafos: I gave the talk and built the attendee kit: an open source agent with a free model builds a complete obby inside Roblox Studio through its MCP server, with map, scripts, shop, power-ups and checkpoints, from fourteen prompts in Spanish.
The kit includes the agent's working rules, four reusable Roblox skills and install guides for Windows, macOS and Linux. I rehearsed the demo timing every prompt so it fit in 45 minutes.

proyectos.tipo: Commercial game developed with AI agents · Steam & Google Play
parrafos: Bubble Hero is developed with Claude Code agents as part of the team: 349 of its 532 commits are co-authored with Claude models.

I set up an art director subagent, an overnight agent that works alone until morning on its own branch with emergency exits, and local transcription of player sessions with Whisper, so the audio never leaves the machine.

proyectos.tipo: AI tablet app · with Ecopetrol & UPB · December 2024 to March 2025
parrafos: For the Ecovilla 4D tablet app I built a voice assistant that answers visitors' questions about the sustainable house of the future.
The visitor speaks, Whisper transcribes, the assistant answers through the OpenAI Assistants API on gpt-4o-mini, and the answer is read aloud with text to speech, all inside Unity.

A task manager on Firestore shared in real time by people and AI agents. I wrote its MCP server in TypeScript, with ten tools to list, create, comment, split into steps and check activity, plus a log of which agent made each change. Claude Code, a phone agent and other assistants use it every day.

For the phone I built a dependency-free version that talks to the Firestore REST API by signing the JWT by hand: it saves 110 MB of dependencies and 107 MB of memory per session, and adds Google Calendar tools.

A toolkit that routes work across several models by cost: my own MCP server that delegates mechanical tasks to Gemini Flash, registered in Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex; scripts that measure each provider's remaining quota; and Amazon Bedrock access through boto3 to run Claude and Qwen3 Coder on credits.
Claude Code hooks and skills remind agents to delegate. I measured before deciding: on the same coding challenges, Gemini Flash used about 0% of the quota versus 30% for a large model.

An agent running on an Android phone with OpenClaw that serves a household over WhatsApp: it checks and creates tasks, manages calendar events and keeps accounts, through the task manager's MCP server.
It runs on Anthropic and Amazon Bedrock models chained as fallbacks, understands images and runs scheduled jobs.
I served Qwen 27B locally with llama.cpp, split across an RTX 5070 and an RTX 3070, and exposed it to agents as an MCP tool. The split took it from 2.6 tokens per second on a single card to 25.5.
I retired it after comparing it with cloud models: with an 8,192-token context and lower accuracy on game engine code, delegating was the better choice.

proyectos.titulo: Character voices with local speech synthesis
parrafos: A pipeline that generates many takes of each line with Chatterbox, transcribes them with Whisper and keeps the best by text fidelity and pacing, to voice the characters of a branded Roblox game.
I also compared Kokoro and Piper, and fine-tuned a voice conversion model (Seed-VC) on a custom dataset.

An agent directs and records the cinematics and trailer of a Roblox game from outside the engine: it moves the camera and characters through the Roblox Studio MCP server, records each shot on a virtual monitor and edits the result.

A web app to practice spoken technical English, with a playable screening interview, rubric and voice, and zero external requests: Whisper recognizes speech and Kokoro synthesizes the voice, both inside the browser on WebGPU.

I generated eleven 3D models with Meshy AI to replace placeholder geometry in a Roblox horror game, and built a Roblox-ready low-poly gargoyle with Python scripts and the Blender MCP server, at 3,924 triangles with 1024 textures.
